checks.message: Neptune cluster storage not encrypted
checks.context: Encryption must be set at creation time — you can't enable it later. Neptune stores graph data that often includes sensitive relationship and identity data.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled
checks.context: Without it, the entire cluster can be destroyed with one command. Enable it on any cluster holding production data.

checks.message: Audit logging not configured
checks.context: Without audit logs you have no record of who queried the graph or what data was accessed. Required for compliance and incident response.

checks.message: No final snapshot specified: Neptune cluster will be deleted without a backup
checks.context: Neptune cluster deletion is permanent. Use --final-db-snapshot-identifier to preserve the graph data.

checks.message: Explicitly skipping final snapshot. All graph data will be permanently lost
checks.context: With --skip-final-snapshot, no backup is taken before deletion. All graph data is gone forever.

checks.message: DocumentDB cluster storage not encrypted
checks.context: Encryption must be set at creation time. DocumentDB clusters often store application data including user records — encrypt at rest.

checks.message: Deletion protection not enabled
checks.context: A single delete command can wipe the entire cluster. Enable it on any cluster holding production data.

checks.message: Audit logging not configured
checks.context: Without audit and profiler logs you have no record of who connected or what operations ran.

checks.message: No final snapshot specified: DocumentDB cluster will be deleted without a backup
checks.context: DocumentDB cluster deletion is permanent. Specify --final-db-snapshot-identifier to preserve the data.

checks.message: Explicitly skipping final snapshot. All document data will be permanently lost
checks.context: With --skip-final-snapshot, no backup is taken before deletion. All DocumentDB data is gone forever.

checks.message: QLDB ledger not encrypted with a customer managed KMS key
checks.context: QLDB uses an AWS-owned key by default. For ledgers storing financial or compliance data, specify --kms-key with a CMK ARN so you have an audit trail of every access and can revoke access independently. Note: QLDB reached end of life on July 31, 2025 and is no longer available — migrate to an alternative service.

checks.message: QLDB ledger deletion destroys the entire immutable transaction history
checks.context: The audit log is QLDB's entire value. Export the journal to S3 before deleting if you need to retain the history for compliance.

checks.message: Verify the instance is not being made publicly accessible or moved to a public subnet
checks.context: DocumentDB instances should remain in private subnets. Making them publicly accessible exposes your document database to internet-based attacks.

checks.message: Verify you are not disabling deletion protection or audit logging
checks.context: Disabling deletion protection on a production Neptune cluster exposes it to accidental deletion. Disabling audit logs removes visibility into graph queries and access patterns.

checks.message: Parameter changes may weaken audit logging or security settings
checks.context: Modifying parameters like neptune_enforce_ssl or audit log settings affects all clusters using this parameter group. Disabling SSL enforcement allows unencrypted connections to your graph database.

checks.message: Verify the instance class change doesn't cause performance degradation during modification
checks.context: Instance class changes trigger a brief failover. If modifying the writer instance, all write operations fail during the switchover. Schedule changes during maintenance windows.

checks.message: Verify you are enabling PITR, not disabling it
checks.context: Point-in-Time Recovery allows restoration to any second within the last 35 days. Disabling PITR removes this protection immediately — if data is corrupted or deleted after disabling, recovery is only possible from on-demand backups. Never disable PITR on production tables.

checks.message: Verify the restored table's billing mode, encryption, and stream settings match your requirements
checks.context: Restored tables may not inherit all settings from the source table. Verify the billing mode (on-demand vs provisioned), SSE configuration, and DynamoDB Streams settings are correct before routing application traffic to the restored table.

checks.message: Verify the restore point is before the data corruption or deletion event
checks.context: Point-in-time restores create a new table — they do not overwrite the existing one. Verify the restore time is before the incident occurred. The restored table will not have the same auto-scaling policies, TTL settings, or CloudWatch alarms as the source.

checks.message: Verify the S3 destination bucket has appropriate encryption and access controls
checks.context: DynamoDB exports write your entire table in JSON or ION format to S3. If the destination bucket is misconfigured (public, wrong KMS key, or overly permissive bucket policy), your entire table data is exposed. Verify the bucket's Block Public Access, encryption, and access policy before exporting.

checks.message: Verify the import source S3 data is from a trusted location and has not been tampered with
checks.context: DynamoDB table imports read data from S3 and create a new table. If the S3 source data has been modified by an unauthorized party, the imported table will contain malicious or incorrect data. Verify the S3 object integrity before importing.

checks.message: Adding or removing replicas affects data availability across regions
checks.context: Adding a replica replicates all existing data to the new region, which can take time for large tables. Removing a replica deletes all data in that region permanently. Verify the change is intentional and that applications in the affected region are prepared for the transition.
